North West Zama Wars

By: Graham Coetzer | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We bring you an exclusive look inside the Zama wars happening in the North West province, where hundreds of armed zamas enter mines at night and the police are powerless to stop it.

Summary:
The Klerksdorp/Stilfontein mining area is literally under attack by illegal miners. Security personnel are shot at on a weekly basis, Zamas scale the headgear of mine shafts from where they snipe at either security staff or rival zamas, and in an incident this week police in armored cars were told to withdraw from a mine at 3 in the morning because the situation was too dangerous. There is literally a fatal shooting in the area every other week. The zama syndicates operating in these areas are not only after illegally mined gold - they are also some of the main players in the copper theft arena. We have footage and video available of how zamas attack an Eskom substation at night, set it on fire and destroy all the equipment within. This means that they can come back the following night and strip the substation of any valuable metals - mostly copper cables etc. The mines are powerless to prevent the theft even though they know when and where it's going to happen because the zamas arrive in large armed groups. Police are usually asked to be at the scene but either fail to arrive or do not have the capacity to deal with the attacks themselves.

Further information:
We have footage available from different sources which shows:
Zama syndicates arriving on a mine at night, literally hundreds, armed to the teeth with AK47's, R5's etc.
Police vehicles being used to deliver illegal copper cable (shiny bright) to scrap dealers in the area
Various zama activities on mines, high voltage power cables etc at night filmed with night vision cameras.

Because we do not have a presenter available for this week, I am going down to Klerksdorp tomorrow 05 August with a cameraman, we will overnight in Klerksdorp. We will be accompanying the |Buffels mine's security division tomorrow night in an armored vehicle as they patrol the mine. The chances are very high that we will get to see the extent of the zamas and how they infiltrate the mines. Once we have this footage we can then return next week with a presenter and cover any outstanding interviews, links and confrontation with SAPS.

Press Release:


Zama Wars
Exclusive CCTV footage shows the shocking extent to which Zama Zamas are wreaking havoc in the North West province. These illegal miners are better known for descending on abandoned mines to get at any gold remaining underground. But North West police and security forces are no match for hundreds of Zamas, armed to the teeth, nightly pillaging local mine infrastructure above ground. Carte Blanche enters the warzone.


Script:


NORTH WEST ZAMA WARS

August 19 2015

2nd draft Script

Voice

This is the Buffels gold mine, located in Stilfontein on the goldfields of the

Witwatersrand basin. The mine, owned by Village Main Reef, is currently one of the

few South African mines undergoing a full rehabilitation.

Sound Up Corne

As mining companies we make a contribution towards a closure fund, and then at

the closure of the mine, these funds are really then just employed to take the mine

back in time, as if what it looked like before mining took place in the area.

Voice

General Manager Corne Strydom says their rehabilitation efforts are being

hampered by often violent attacks on the mine by illegal miners known as Zama

Zamas.

Sound Up Corne

The rehabilitation area is the one mostly affected by Zama Zama activity.

Voice

23 January 2015. It’s about two minutes past one in the morning, and a truck

carrying gold ore is about to make a delivery to the mine at Stilfontein in the North

West province. Both mine security and the driver are unaware that armed Zama

Zamas have hitched a ride on the back of the trailer.

Sound Up Music

Voice

They overpower the guard, taking him hostage. Almost immediately more men

emerge from the darkness and together they make their way to a part of the mine

where ore-bearing material is processed. The masked man seen here is monitoring

mine security’s radio communications. The men quickly loot the plant, and when

security arrives the Zamas make a hostile retreat.

Sound Up Johan

Basically every night, they will come into these areas and try and pick whatever they

can… Our losses are in the region of fifty million a month.

Voice

Since the closure of the Buffels mine, Zamas in the area no longer bother spending

days below ground illegally mining for gold. For the past few months they have

simply entered the mine and stolen anything of value, particularly copper and steel

which they sell to dodgy scrap dealers.

Link Devi

This is number 2 Shaft. It was closed a month ago, and a week ago a concrete slab

was put over the hole. But we’ve just arrived here with mine security and it’s clear

that this is an active operation. There are trucks that’s transporting steel out of here

and there’s even a little tuck shop. For these Zama Zamas it’s business as usual.

Sound Up Johan

These guys, all they are actually trying to do is to put food on the table for their next

of kin.

Voice

Buffels mine manager Johan Hennop says the group of Zamas who enter the mine by

day are for the most part docile and non violent.

Sound Up Johan

Then on the other side, the other group is really the violent group, and they

normally move around at night time only, also with weapons and shooting on the

guys with live ammunition.

Link Devi

Behind me is Ten Shaft, by day it’s all calm - it looks perfectly normal as contractors

are busy rehabilitating the mine, but by night, this turns into a complete warzone.

Voice

This footage, captured by mine CCTV cameras, shows more than a hundred zamas in

the bush next to the mine. Once they gain access to the property it’s literally a free

for all as they descend on 10 Shaft, and strip every bit of valuable copper or steel.

The zamas are often armed with an assortment of high caliber machine guns,

shotguns and even hunting rifles equipped with scopes.

Sound Up Corne

So as soon as a confrontation issue where violence and shots are fired we try and

contain, but largely we move away; given the sensitivity associated post Marikana.

Voice

That makes security’s job all the more difficult – containing the zamas to a certain

area often results in cat and mouse games with armed groups who find ample hiding

places in the abandoned buildings and veldt on mine property.

Sound Up Johan

It’s very difficult to understand, will these people attack? Must we apprehend? Must

we rather pull back and just observe?

Voice

But in recent months the zamas have become more brazen. This footage captured

earlier this month shows a group of armed zamas attacking the security barracks.

While these men keep an eye on security the rest of the group make away with

bulletproof vests and security uniforms which they promptly equip themselves with

a little later in a nearby veldt.

Sound Up Johan

In the past we had a couple of real bad incidents where the guys have been shot on…

and it’s very difficult for the guys they never know what to expect next.

Voice

We decided to spend a few evenings on patrol with mine security to get a feel for the

situation on the ground.

Link Devi

This entire mine is monitored by close onto a 140 cameras 24/7. So when we go on

patrol tonight, big brother will be watching.

Voice

And it soon became apparent that our first night out would not be a quiet one…

Sound Up Dewald

We received a call from our control room, the CCTV control room, that there is

between 50 and 60 people, zama zamas currently busy at number ten shaft.



Sound Up Devi

We’re headed now to 10 Shaft and while I do feel relatively safe because this is an

armored vehicle; a stark reminder for me is the bullet holes in the window – things

can go wrong.

Sound Up Devi

Initially as you drive through this particular piece of the mine everything seems

quiet, but it seems that every single corner that you take you’ll find a group of

people running in the opposite direction and all they are, are shadows in the night.

Voice

On a second night spent with security we found large groups of zamas burning

copper next to 10 shaft. Security spotted two bakkies driving without their lights

and gave chase.

Sound Up Chase

Voice

With the bakkies leaving the area, we returned to where a large group of zamas had

gathered in the veldt. None of the Zamas seemed armed and we were about to leave

when the reality of just how dangerous these kinds of patrols can be hit home.

Several gunshots rang out in the night.

Sound Up Shooting

Voice

Security returned fire using a shotgun with rubber bullets before we withdrew from

the area.

Sound Up Dewald

We’re here at the back of number 10 shaft in the old hostel area where one shot

were fired at the vehicle that hit the vehicle at the right hand side at the back.

Voice

Back in the relative safety of the screening plant we informed police of the incident.

Luckily we were in the armored vehicle as soft skinned vehicles like this one are

simply sitting ducks…

Sound Up Johan

Johan: And this is where we fall back onto the defense of the police and we ask them

to come and help us and assist us with those kind of attacks.

Voice

Major General Patrick Asaneng is the cluster commander for the Klerksdorp Cluster,

which includes seven local police stations in the area. He admits that the Zama

problem is a serious one.

Sound Up General Asaneng

Devi: How bad is the issue of zama zamas – specifically in Stilfontein?

General: It is bad, especially when it also involves loss of lives attacks.

Voice

He says the situation is exacerbated by rivalries between different zama gangs.

Sound Up General Asaneng

They are prepared to shoot to kill. They are rival groups, but as a result of them

being involved in these turf wars they would also then attack the private securities

that are employed by the mine.

Voice

The Buffels mine spans just over 12000 hectares of land. A drive through the area

reveals the devastating extent of Zama vandalism committed over past months.

Sound Up Johan

It was quite a big area, a big village, a hundred houses, we also had a nursery school

here where we accommodated the local children with a soccer field and sport

facilities on my left hand side but as you can see everything has been vandalized and

is not operable anymore.

Voice

Johan feels the police aren’t controlling or bringing the Zamas to book.

Sound Up Johan

Devi: The police, are they helpful?

Johan: In general they do assist, but I am just of the opinion that we don’t get

support, the way we are supposed to get it, from the police.

Sound Up General

Devi: It becomes your problem in the end even if there is private security and even if

they need to look after their own goods and you can only do so much, the buck will

still stop with you.

General: That’s why I m admitting and saying, I will not abrogate my constitutional

duty and responsibility the buck stops with the police.

Link Devi

23 mines used to operate in this area, now there are only three. Thousands of

people have lost their jobs, there are deep social issues which cannot be ignored

here. In many cases, zama zamas are just trying to put food on the table.

Sound Up Dorothy

They struggle, they struggle. They lend money they can’t pay back. They sit there at

home, some are dying of hunger.

Voice

Dorothy Matlakala lives in the Khuma township near Buffels. She says a family

friend who had joined a group of zamas to earn a living was killed during a shootout

between rival gangs.

Sound Up Dorothy

The friend of Tebogo, they phoned him, and said the owner of this phone, you

should not say he is still alive, you should know he is dead. It’s sad, sad.

Voice Graham

The South African mining sector faces mine closures and mass retrenchments. And,

with the authorities seemingly unable to curb the Zama Zama onslaught, scenes of

criminality likes these continue to endanger lives and mar the mining landscape.

This means that they can come back the following night and strip the substation of any valuable metals - mostly copper cables etc. The mines are powerless to prevent the theft even though they know when and where it's going to happen because the zamas arrive in large armed groups. Police are usually asked to be at the scene but either fail to arrive or do not have the capacity to deal with the attacks themselves.
metadata.Further information: We have footage available from different sources which shows: Zama syndicates arriving on a mine at night, literally hundreds, armed to the teeth with AK47's, R5's etc. Police vehicles being used to deliver illegal copper cable (shiny bright) to scrap dealers in the area Various zama activities on mines, high voltage power cables etc at night filmed with night vision cameras. Because we do not have a presenter available for this week, I am going down to Klerksdorp tomorrow 05 August with a cameraman, we will overnight in Klerksdorp. We will be accompanying the |Buffels mine's security division tomorrow night in an armored vehicle as they patrol the mine. The chances are very high that we will get to see the extent of the zamas and how they infiltrate the mines. Once we have this footage we can then return next week with a presenter and cover any outstanding interviews, links and confrontation with SAPS.
